$comment: What's new in Pocket Fishing Guide, for anglers and guides: the angler-facing cut of CHANGELOG.md, one entry per change a person can see or use. Newest first. `areas` is the map of the app's parts (id, label, a wb-icons icon, the part's home `href`, the path prefixes it `match`es); every entry names one in `area`. An optional `image` is a capture of the part on a phone (`src` under /assets/whats-new/, `alt` in plain words, `width`/`height` of the file, `page` the same-origin path it was captured from, an optional `selector`), made by web/scripts/capture-whats-new.mjs. Validated by scripts/validate-whats-new.js; mirrored at web/lib/data/whats-new.json (the bundle) and web/public/data/whats-new.json (served at /data/whats-new.json, read by talewatersandtides.com/news/). Rules: AGENTS.md (web) 'What's new'; runbook docs/runbooks/whats-new.md.

entries.title: Change a fishing day and keep the conversation going
entries.body: Reschedule or cancel a buddy plan, compare shared days and weather at the trip’s water, and reply to or like a message. New updates appear while you stay on a page. Device alerts are opt-in in Settings; sound follows your phone’s settings.

entries.title: See the week at the dam again
entries.body: The recovered October 23 read now shows its hourly dam history, October year wheel and guide illustration. Meet Buffalo Outdoor Center in a complimentary partner spotlight, with its profile photo and a link to plan a Buffalo River trip.

entries.title: Find your next Friday Read and share a link
entries.body: Move between fishing news, water editions and earlier weeks. Share a story or edition with your phone’s share sheet, or copy its link. Earlier editions still ask visitors to sign in for the full read.

entries.title: October 23’s Friday Read is back on Bull Shoals
entries.body: Read the recovered Bull Shoals Tailwater email from October 23, with its original editorial text and a historical notice. Personal details and unverified images are omitted. Archive loading errors now say when the archive is unavailable.

entries.title: Share what you see at the water
entries.body: Report rising water, a blocked ramp or a change at your access. Add a photo, like or share a report, and follow a place or incident for in-app updates. Each observation keeps its source and time.

image.alt: A river scene above the condition report controls, with a choice of water and a place to share what an angler sees.

entries.title: Post your catch without waiting for review
entries.body: Accept the updated content agreement and your catch and photos post right away. Report a photo to hide that image until a steward reviews it. The catch and its other photos stay posted.

entries.title: This one got away
entries.body: Buddy greets you when a page cannot be found, with links to explore waters or go home so you can get back to planning your time on the water.

entries.title: Find an outfitter from home
entries.body: Browse guides, boat rentals, shuttles and places to stay from home. Meet Buffalo Outdoor Center in the home cards, with a link to its profile for rates and trip details.

entries.title: Check for new days, any time
entries.body: Guides whose open days come from their own calendar now get a Check for new days button on their page and on Set up your listing. Anglers can tap it too. Mark a day open in your calendar, tap it, and the day shows. The calendar is still read once a day on its own.

entries.title: Settings is shorter, and saves as you tap
entries.body: Settings now holds your name, your emails, who sees what and how the app talks to you. Each switch saves the moment you tap it, so there is no Save button to miss. Your waters, fish and how you fish are on your profile.

entries.title: Change your waters and fish on your profile
entries.body: Your profile now has a What I fish card: your home water and the others you fish, your top five fish, and how and when you go. Tap Edit on a row to change it right there, with the same picks you saw when you set up.

entries.title: Planned a day? Ask who's going
entries.body: Once you plan a day from the home calendar, the sheet offers one link for a buddy. The text names the day and the water, so they know what you are asking. Not now hides it for a month.

entries.title: Know a guide or a club? Tell us
entries.body: Where a water has no guide listed, or a part of the state has no club yet, you can now tell us who to call. Give the name and town, and tick the box if we may say you sent us. We reach out ourselves.

entries.title: Pick all your waters and your top fish
entries.body: Setting up now takes up to five waters: your home water first, then the others you fish, which land in your saved waters. Your fish come picked from those waters, top fish first. Tap to change them, up to five.

entries.title: An email when an angler asks for a trip
entries.body: Guides and outfitters who run their page here now get an email the moment an angler asks for a day or a plan of days: what they asked for, when, the posted price and where their message went, with one tap to your desk. Turn it off in Settings under Trip requests.

entries.title: See every welcome card
entries.body: The welcome cards at the top of home now open up: See more shows every card we made, from the dam and river levels to clubs, and Show fewer folds it back. New here? The cards sit under the greeting with Join free and Sign in, and the clarity card opens the lure color tool itself.

entries.title: Booking a guide shows what else is on that morning
entries.body: When you pick a day and a trip in a guide's booking panel, it now says if you're already in a club outing, a buddy plan or another guide trip that morning, afternoon or day. Fine if this one's a backup: it's a heads-up and the request still goes.

entries.title: One fishing plan a day with each buddy
entries.body: If you and a buddy already have a plan for a day, asking again opens that plan instead of starting a second one, and a plan can't be moved onto that day. A plan either of you said no to leaves the day free.

entries.title: Welcome cards on home, each season
entries.body: Cards at the top of home: your water's best time to go, then three that change with the day and season, from the dam and river levels to lure colors, the moon and bringing a friend. Each opens the real page. Hide this puts them away until next season, with no pop-up, and Settings turns them off.

entries.title: One way in: Sign in or Join free
entries.body: The menu, the sign-in box and every button now use the same words: Sign in, Join free and Sign out. One email does both, new or returning. On the home page, a card under today's read says what joining keeps: your home water first, your plans and your people.

entries.title: See when two plans land on one morning
entries.body: Coming up on the water now flags a buddy plan, club outing or guide trip on the same morning, afternoon or day as something you're in or waiting on, and the outing or buddy plan says so above your answer. A heads-up, not a block: you can still fish two things in a day.

entries.title: Club news in fewer taps
entries.body: Answer a new outing from Waiting for you and its club's badge clears with the answer, so Your clubs only shows what you haven't seen. Clubs & Events in the menu now opens Your clubs when you're signed in.

entries.title: Your clubs, one place
entries.body: Your clubs now sit together with their days: each club is a card with its next outing, and a badge says when something new waits there until you open it. Mine and Across Arkansas switch between your club days and every public club's. The menu shows where you are.

entries.title: Team of the Year, for anyone to read
entries.body: A club with public standings now shows Team of the Year there too: its season teams by points over each team event's final board, named as the team chose. An angler on a team is named only by their own choice. Teams lists each public season's leading team.

entries.title: Divisions on a club event
entries.body: A club event can have divisions, kayak and boat or boater and co-angler say. Pick yours under Enter; the board stays one board, and All · Kayak · Boat shows each division's own places. An officer can fix anyone's division at the ramp.

entries.title: A season team gets its own page
entries.body: Every season team has a page in its club: its logo, a cover photo and a line about the team, the roster, where it stands in Team of the Year, its place on each final board and its longest fish. The team's lead or the club's owner and admins set the look; tap a team's name on the season or the club's page to open it.

entries.title: Clear away days that didn't happen
entries.body: On Your club days, a day's ··· (or a swipe left on a phone) hides it from your days, with Undo; a hidden day comes back if the club changes it. Called-off days fold into Earlier with the days behind. A club's owner or admin can delete a club event nobody else entered.

entries.title: Find yourself on a big board
entries.body: A club event's board now leads with your place, your total and how far the line above you is, with Jump to me. Search a name, narrow to a team or reorder by the longest fish, and on a team event switch between Teams and Anglers. On a wide screen an angler's fish open beside the board.

entries.title: A club's teams on its page
entries.body: A club's page now lists the teams on its open seasons, with who is on each. Your own team comes first, and a team that asked you on says so.

entries.title: Teams has its own page
entries.body: Clubs & Events has a Teams row: your season teams and event teams in one place, then the Team clubs across Arkansas and their sponsors. The day rows now read Your club days and Club days across Arkansas.

entries.title: Season teams and Team of the Year
entries.body: A club's season can now have teams of up to four members. On each team event of the season, tap Fish with your team to join that day's boat, and the season's page keeps Team of the Year from the final boards.

entries.title: Join a team with its link or code
entries.body: On a club event fished as teams, share your team's link or its 8-letter code and partners join at once while there is room. Or ask a team with room to let you in, and its lead says yes or no.

entries.title: Fish a club event as a team
entries.body: Officers can now make a club event for teams of one to four, two by default. Start a team on the event, ask a partner from the entrants, guests too, and your team's best fish count together on the board.

entries.title: Bring a guest to a club event
entries.body: Officers can now send a guest link from a club event. Someone not in the club makes a free account, confirms they're 18 or older and is entered on that event only: the event, its board and where to meet, never the club's members or other days.

entries.title: Pick the picture on your club's page and on an outing
entries.body: A club's owner and admins can now give the club's cover, or any outing, one of our scenes, from foggy mornings and tailwaters to bass boats, underwater shots and bait, or upload a photo. An outing's picture runs behind its day and water; with none, it shows the water's scene as before.

entries.title: Pick the water in your tank and the picture behind your name
entries.body: Tank scene picks the water every tank you look at swims in, yours, your buddies', your clubs' and each water's: clear water, a trout run, a catfish hole or a moonlit lake, its own fish beside yours. The camera on your cover now offers our scenes too, from foggy mornings to bass boats and bait, or your own photo.

entries.title: Guided trips on your calendar, and each kind its own colour
entries.body: Guided trips now ride in your calendar subscription with the business, the trip and the price as posted or quoted. Subscribe one calendar per kind to give guided trips, club days, buddy plans and saved plans their own colours. Guides get their bookings too.

entries.title: Your fishing days on your phone's calendar, kept up to date
entries.body: Subscribe once from Coming up on your profile and your club outings, club events, buddy plans and saved plans show in Apple or Google Calendar. When an outing moves or is called off, your calendar changes too. Get a new link or turn it off any time.

entries.title: Your next day on the water, at the top of every page
entries.body: A calendar now sits beside Saved and the camera whenever a club outing, a club event or a buddy plan you both said yes to is in the next two weeks. It counts them and lights up on the day. Add to calendar on an outing or a buddy plan now opens in Calendar on an iPhone, no sign-in.

entries.title: An estimated weight, filled in from the length
entries.body: Log a fish's length on a fishing report and the weight fills itself in, about how much a fish that long weighs, from the published standard weight for that species and labelled an estimate. Weighed it? Type the weight and say how: a hand scale or a certified scale.

entries.title: Anglers and club bests on your club
entries.body: Your club's page now keeps score across every finalized club event: each angler's events, fish counted and finishes, and the club's longest fish of each kind with who caught it and where. Officers can download the anglers as a CSV file.

entries.title: Keep a club event's board and attendance
entries.body: Officers can now print a club event's sheet or save it as a PDF, and download the board and the attendance as CSV files for a spreadsheet. A series' standings download the same way. The paid column is your own note, and no email, phone or place is in any file.

entries.title: Add the catch's photo to a fishing report
entries.body: Posting a fishing report now takes the catch's photos too, up to three, so a report with a photo is a catch in your tank, verified by the photo where it can be. Post tells you what is still missing instead of staying grey, and Log a catch got a cleaner look.

entries.title: Tap anyone on a club event's board
entries.body: On a club event, tap any angler on the board to see the fish behind their total: each counted fish with its photo, length and the judges' word. Officers get judging first when catches wait, a quicker roster at the ramp and a bigger board photo with the day's word on it.

entries.title: A welcome on the clubs, and shared links that make sense
entries.body: New to Pocket Fishing Guide? The clubs pages now say what the app is and what a club does here. A public club's page shows its days coming up to anyone. A shared club event or outing link now opens the club's page and says how to join, instead of a sign-in box.

entries.title: Club events for trout on the tailwaters
entries.body: A club can now run a catch-photo-release event for trout on an Arkansas tailwater. Each catch names the nearest AGFC access, seen only by the angler and the judges, who also see that day's rules there. A best-brown ladder sits beside the board, and every fish goes back.

entries.title: Businesses can offer to sponsor a club
entries.body: A guide service, outfitter or shop with a listing can now offer to back a public club from the club's page. The club's officers say yes or not now, and the business can take the offer back while it waits. Our own guide service can be a club's sponsor too, always named as ours. No money moves through the app.

entries.title: Clubs and club events are for anglers 18 and older
entries.body: Starting, joining or following a club, answering an outing and entering a club event now ask once that you're 18 or older. If you're already in a club, you'll be asked the next time you do one of those. Buddies stay open from 13, and you can always leave a club.

entries.title: See what clubs are fishing, and where
entries.body: Clubs & Events has a new Club days ahead page: every public club's outings and club events for the next three months, by day and water, with a map and filters. Open one to follow the club or ask to join.

entries.title: The trout rules for today, on every tailwater
entries.body: On a trout water's page, License & Regulations now says what's in force today: which areas are closed or catch-and-release, the daily limit since February, and what changes later in the year. Below the Ouachita dams it also says when trout are stocked.

entries.title: Your latest catches, one tap away
entries.body: Your profile now opens your newest catches in a strip above your tanks: the photo, the day, the water and whether it's approved or still in review. Tap one to see the whole catch and share it.

entries.title: See what's waiting before you tap
entries.body: The number beside your picture now opens a short list of what it is: buddy requests, fishing plans, new buddies, club outings and events. Each line says who and what, and takes you straight there.

entries.title: Heavy hitters and the longest fish, beside the points
entries.body: A club's season now keeps two more races under its standings: every counted inch over the season, and the longest single fish. An officer can name one event the Classic and weigh it, or count only each angler's best scores.

entries.title: What the weigh-ins say about a water
entries.body: A water's Reports tab now shows what AGFC's tournament program reported for it last season: how many weigh-ins, who weighed a fish, the average bass and the best months. Counts only, from the agency's own report.

entries.title: Angler reports, with their catch
entries.body: Each angler report on a water now shows the fish on its own underwater scene, easier to read on a phone. An approved report opens its catch's page, with the photo.

entries.title: Share your catch
entries.body: Right after you post, Share the catch sends your photo with the fish and the water to a text or a post. Once a catch is approved, it has its own page with a picture card, and you can share it from your tank.

entries.title: Your catch, front and center
entries.body: After you post a catch, the snap sheet now shows your photo as the hero, with the fish and the water you caught it on. A business that works that water may show its logo in the corner, and a club that fishes the water is one tap away.

entries.title: See where your club fishes
entries.body: A club outing's plan now shows its water on the map of Arkansas. A season shows every water its events fished, and a club's public standings show where they fish. Tap a water's name to read it.

entries.title: Clubs show the next step clearly
entries.body: Club pages, outings and club events now highlight one next step at a time. Your answer to an outing and each check-in show as a calm selection, and links to the board or the standings look like links, not big buttons.

entries.title: Pick your catch by its photo
entries.body: Submitting a catch to a club event now shows your snaps from the outing as photo tiles. Tap the fish you want counted, and the length you logged fills in for you to check against the board.

entries.title: See the catches waiting on you to judge
entries.body: If you run a club, the catches waiting on you to judge now show first on Outings & events and on your club's page, with how many each club event has. Tap one to open its judging, with the photos.

entries.title: Watch how it's done from the outing drawing
entries.body: The drawing on a club outing's How to fish that day now has a Watch button. It opens a how-to video for the technique shown, filmed on that water when we have one, on YouTube.

entries.title: See where the fish hold before you go
entries.body: How to fish that day on a club outing now opens on a drawing of the water: the riffle, seam, run and pool on a river, or the flat, point and drop-off on a lake, with your water's lead fish where it holds for the season. Where to meet and who's going have their own card.

entries.title: Outings show the team and how to fish the day
entries.body: A club outing now opens with the team's logo and its sponsors, the date at the top, and Add to calendar on its own row. Below your answer, How to fish that day gives the weather, the moon, the technique and what to throw on that water.

entries.title: Find clubs and club days on the map
entries.body: The clubs list and your Outings & events now open with the Fish Arkansas map: each water with a club or a club day is a dot sized by how many. Tap one to see only that water's clubs or days, then read the water from its card.

entries.title: Days wear their season, and long lists filter
entries.body: Every date tile now wears its season: ice blue in winter, green in spring, gold in summer, amber in fall, with a small glyph, and today is ringed. Outings & events and an event's ramp roster get search and filters once they grow long.

entries.title: Club events look like your club
entries.body: A club event, a season's standings and the public board now open on your club's picture and mark. The top three stand on a podium with the fish that leads, every angler shows their own mark, and officers get one row of jumps to what waits on them.

entries.title: A clearer path from your profile to a fishing day
entries.body: Fishing plans now opens from a clear row on your profile. Buddy rows lead with the next day you share, tablet navigation is more compact, and outings show their water's scene with the day's conditions separate from the meeting time.

entries.title: Your clubs' week in the Friday email
entries.body: The Friday email now lists this week's outings and club events of the clubs you're in, with your own answer beside each, and of the clubs you follow, by day and water. A club you muted stays out of it.

entries.title: Follow a club you're not in
entries.body: On a public club's page, tap Follow and its outings and club events ahead show on your Outings & events, by day and water. The club sees how many follow it, never who, and nobody is told when you follow or stop.

entries.title: A club's standings, for anyone to see
entries.body: A public club can now show its final boards and its season's standings to anyone at its standings page, with a share button. Your name shows there only if you say so when you enter an event; otherwise you read as "An angler" with your place kept.

entries.title: The season's standings, and a two-day club event
entries.body: A club's events can be a series now: a two-day event adds up each day's final board, and a season gives points by placing with the lowest scores dropped. Officers start one from the club page; the standings come from final boards only, so a running board never moves them.

entries.title: Run a club event from your phone, start to finish
entries.body: Officers can change the rules until the first catch is in, check anglers in at the ramp, note who paid, take someone off with a reason, call it off with a word everyone reads, and reopen a final board for seven days to fix a mistake. Entrants can say I'm out and come back. A How to run it card shows the step you're on.

entries.title: Clubs & Events on the menu, and your club days in one list
entries.body: The menu's Clubs item is now Clubs & Events: all clubs, Outings & events, and Start a club. Outings & events lists every outing and club event ahead across your clubs, soonest first, with where you stand on each; a club you run gets a Plan an outing door. The clubs page says what running a club here gets you.

entries.title: A club event's tank keeps the fish
entries.body: Under the board, the event's tank: every fish the judges counted, each kind drawn at its longest board length, with the tally. Tap a fish to see who caught it, the board length, the photo and the judges' word. Entrants see names and photos here; the club's own tank keeps counts only.

entries.title: Log a catch from anywhere
entries.body: Signed in, the gold button at the bottom right is now Log a catch, on every page; feedback sits just above it. There is a camera in the top bar too, and a new angler gets a Log a catch door right after setting up. Snap the fish, post, keep fishing.

entries.title: A club outing can be a catch-photo-release event
entries.body: An officer makes a planned outing a club event: best N fish by length, a minimum, a word to write on the board. Members enter, snap each fish on the board from the water, let it go and submit the catch; the officers judge the photos and the board ranks everyone. Finalize freezes it and every entrant is told.

entries.title: Tap a fish, see the catch
entries.body: A caught fish in your tank now wears a small camera chip: tap it to see each catch — the day, the water, the size, Released or Kept, what worked, the photo and how it was verified. A buddy’s catches open the same sheet when they share them. The fish itself still logs a catch.

entries.title: Share a photo straight to the app, or post with no signal
entries.body: On Android, share a fish photo from your camera roll to Pocket Fishing Guide and the catch opens ready to post. Hold the app icon for a Log a catch shortcut. No signal on the water? Post anyway: the catch waits on your phone and sends itself when a bar comes back.

entries.title: What worked, with pictures
entries.body: Once a catch is posted, the lures and techniques that work for that fish on that water show as picture tiles, the season’s lures first and the likely one already lit. One tap confirms or changes it, and it goes on your report. Also on each catch waiting for a name.

entries.title: Snap a photo, post the catch, get back on the fish
entries.body: Log a catch is now the photo first: Post needs nothing else. The app fills in the club outing you are on today, the lake from the photo or your phone (the lake only, never your spot) and the time the photo was taken, each a tap to change. Name the fish now or at the truck from “catches to name” on your tank.

entries.title: Your row on the day bar, in your colour
entries.body: On the day sheet's hour-by-hour bar your own row now wears your avatar colour with a white rim, the way each buddy's row wears theirs, so you can see at a glance whether the bite window lands when you are free.

entries.title: A fishing plan with a buddy reads like an invite
entries.body: Open a plan and the day leads on a calendar tile, with the part of the day and the water beside it. Where it stands sits in one box with what to do next, the answers line up two across, and the thread reads like a chat with the box sending from inside its field.

entries.title: A guide for the day you open
entries.body: Tap a day on your calendar and, when a sponsored guide works that water, the day sheet now shows them with the day as they posted it and their price, one tap to their page with that day picked. The guide whose open day fits the part you marked comes first.

entries.title: Your days, marked on the calendar
entries.body: On your profile's calendar a day with a guide trip, a buddy plan, a club outing or a saved day now wears a folded corner. Tap it and the day sheet lists what is on, each one tap from its page, above the day's read.

entries.title: Everything with a date, in one place
entries.body: Your profile now opens with Coming up on the water: your saved days, guide trips, buddy plans and club outings in one list, soonest first, each with where it stands and one tap to its page. What waits on you is counted at the top.

entries.title: A guide for your club's outing
entries.body: When a club plans a day on the water, the outing's page now offers a guide who works that water, with the day the club picked already chosen on their page. It shows a guide's own words and posted prices, and only where a sponsored guide works that water.

entries.title: A club's page now opens for anyone
entries.body: Share a club's link or find one in the directory and the club itself opens, signed in or not: who it is, its water and today's read, its sponsors and how many are in. Joining still takes an account, so the one door is Sign in to join. Private clubs stay members-only.

entries.title: AGFC's six regions on the Live Waters Map
entries.body: Turn on the Clubs layer and the map now draws AGFC's six fishing-report regions under the club pins, each with its name. Open a region from the clubs directory and the map lands on it with its clubs, and one tap takes you back to all of Arkansas.

entries.title: Live gauges down the White River on the map
entries.body: The map's USGS gauges layer now reads the White below Bull Shoals: near Norfork, Calico Rock, Sylamore, Batesville, Newport, Augusta and DeValls Bluff. Each pin shows the flow in cfs, whether the river is rising, and how long ago the gauge read it.

entries.title: Clubs on the Live Waters Map
entries.body: Turn on the Clubs layer and every water with a club gets a pin, sized by how many anglers fish in its clubs. Tap one to see the clubs on that water and open any of them. From the clubs page, On the map opens the layer for you.

entries.title: A club's link now lands you in the club
entries.body: Say yes to a club's link and the next door opens the club itself, not your Buddies card. Set up your profile first and you still land in the club after. Open a club from the directory signed out and the sign-in box says so. Small fixes across the club pages too.

entries.title: See the clubs across Arkansas
entries.body: Clubs now has its own page in the rail: how many clubs and anglers there are across the state, a tile for each AGFC region with its most-chased fish, and a list you can search and filter by kind, region and water. Open any club to read about it and join.

entries.title: Join your water's club as you sign up
entries.body: The last screen of onboarding now offers the club for the water you picked, with how many anglers are in it. Join with one tap, or Not now and find it on your profile later. Nobody is put in a club without asking.

entries.title: The state records tank swims on the home page
entries.body: Swipe the Fish Arkansas card on the home page to see Arkansas's biggest state record fish in one tank, then the guide for your water and your own water's tank. Tap a fish to open it big with its record, who caught it and when, and a way to fish that water.

entries.title: Your club has a fish tank
entries.body: A club's page now has the club's own fish tank: every fish its members chase, the caught ones leading, with how many the club has logged from approved catch reports. It counts fish, never photos or places, and only from members who show their tank to buddies.

entries.title: Clubs: tinted marks, a cleaner outing page
entries.body: Club marks now carry a letter from the club's name (not "The") and a tint by kind: a crew gold, a club blue, a team green. An outing's page leads with the day and time, with the club named above it. On a wide screen the roster runs in columns.

entries.title: Give your club its own picture, cover and sponsors
entries.body: A club's owner and admins can set its picture and the photo across the top, right on the club's page. The club's line under its name is now one line. A club can name the local business that backs it, and a team up to three; their logos show on the page and open the business's page.

entries.title: Plan the outing on the day most of the club is free
entries.body: When an officer plans an outing, the form now shows the days most of the club marked free, and how many marked the day you picked. It is a count, never a name, and only from members whose free days are set to My buddies. Members on Only me are never counted.

entries.title: Tap any fish in a water's tank, even one behind another
entries.body: On a computer, a fish swimming behind another in a water's tank now opens its own card, and a record fish the Techniques tab doesn't cover offers How to fish it on its species guide. The brown trout card also now says Rip Collins's fish held the world record for 17 years.

entries.title: Report a club, and turn one club's emails off
entries.body: A club page now has Report this club, and every member's row has Report behind its ···; an outing's page has Report this outing. Each one reaches a person at Pocket Fishing Guide. You can also turn off one club's emails from its ··· menu, or from the link at the foot of its emails, and still see everything here.

entries.title: Profiles and clubs lead with the photo, the name beside the picture
entries.body: Your profile, a buddy's card and a club page now open on the cover photo, with the profile picture on its corner and the name beside it; everything else reads below on solid ground. The New buddy, role and kind tags sit together on the photo's top right, and New now shows for a day.

entries.title: Clubs plan outings: pick a day, say I'm in
entries.body: A club now plans a day on the water: an officer picks the day, the part of it, the water, a meeting time and where to meet in words. Everyone in the club hears about it, says I'm in, Maybe or Can't make it, and can add it to their calendar. The evening before, the ones who are in get a reminder.

entries.title: Clubs: start a crew, send one link, see who's in
entries.body: Start a crew, a club or a team from your profile, pick its home water, and send one link for the whole text thread. Whoever opens it sees who asked, where the club fishes and how many are in, and says yes with one tap. Officers let people in, set roles and can hand the club over.

entries.title: The tank shows the state record caught on that water
entries.body: On a computer, a water's tank now marks a fish that holds the Arkansas state record from that water. Open it to see the weight, who caught it and when, from AGFC's record list: the 40 lb 4 oz brown trout on the Little Red, the 64 lb 8 oz striper below Beaver Dam and more.

entries.title: Tap a fish on a water's card to see how to catch it
entries.body: On a water's Signals tab, tap a fish in the Fish Arkansas card and it opens on four swipe cards: its bite window, how deep and where with the top techniques, the lures to throw, and a ready-to-fish tackle box. Tap a technique or a lure for the full how-to.

entries.title: On a computer, a water's tank shows who lives there
entries.body: On a computer, a water's Signals tab now mixes its tank and its top lure in among the partner cards. Tap a fish in the tank and it opens big on its own underwater scene, with its season note, how to tell it apart, a did-you-know and a way to fish it there.

entries.title: Each fish on a water now shows its bite window and how long is left
entries.body: On a water's Signals tab, the Fish Arkansas card now says, for each species, whether it is in a good feeding window and how long is left, or how long until the next one, with its day drawn hour by hour. Plan it opens the forecast, and Share sends the read to a friend.

entries.title: A buddy's ask reaches your email now
entries.body: When a buddy asks to be buddies, says yes, asks you to fish or answers a plan, you get one email with a button that opens it in the app. Turn them off from any of those emails, or under Buddy emails in Settings.

entries.title: The map keeps a dam's read while the Corps update is late
entries.body: The Corps posts each hour's dam reading about an hour late, and the map used to grey the dam card in that gap. It now keeps the units, flow and access-point calls, and says how old the reading is, the same as the dam card.

entries.title: The Friday Read: this week's email, as a page for every water
entries.body: Open Friday Read in the menu for the week on your water: the days to go, how the water ran at the dam, the fish this season and a guide to call. This week's read is open to everyone; with a profile you can read the weeks before it.

entries.title: A What's new icon in the top bar, and one note when something changed
entries.body: When the app changes, the book icon at the top shows how many changes you have not seen, on a phone too. The first page you open after a change shows one short note; close it and the changes count as seen.

entries.title: A Ned rig and a Clouser Minnow join the lure picks
entries.body: Smallmouth bass pages now lead with the Ned rig, the light finesse jig Ozark stream anglers fish on spinning gear, and the Clouser Minnow joins the smallmouth and white bass picks for the fly rod. Each opens to why it works and the water it does best in.

entries.title: Throw this leads with the lures for the season
entries.body: On a water's Techniques tab each fish's lures are now ordered for the season the fish are in, read from today's water temperature. The ones tuned for it come first with an In season now tag, and a line under the heading says which season and what water temperature drove the order.

entries.title: The Friday read sign-up now shows on phones
entries.body: On a phone, a water's Signals tab now offers that water's read every Friday under the read, as it already did on a computer: type your email and tap Go. The Go button is gold again on both.

image.alt: The Friday read sign-up on the White River below Bull Shoals Dam page on a phone: one email a week, stop any time with one tap, an email field and a gold Go button

entries.title: The whole Arkansas River on one card, with a week of release
entries.body: The Arkansas River page now opens with every lock and dam on one strip, like the Buffalo's: the release from the lowest dam to the highest, which pools are rising or falling, and a week of daily release for the pool you tap.

entries.title: Ozark Lake has its own page
entries.body: Ozark Lake, the Arkansas River pool behind Ozark-Jeta Taylor Lock and Dam, now has a page of its own like Lake Dardanelle: its signals, forecast and species, with the lock and dam on the Tailwaters tab.

entries.title: River gauges read live on the map
entries.body: The Live Waters Map's USGS gauges now show what the river is doing: each dot takes its level colour, turns amber while rising and shows its flow. Tap one for a small card with the flow, the change over two hours, and whether to wade or paddle.

entries.title: Make the map bigger
entries.body: On the Live Waters Map, a button beside the zoom controls fills your screen with the map, its card and its legend; press it again or Escape to come back. The dam card's access points now read as a bar, an icon and one word, with the pulse time below.

entries.title: Each Arkansas River pool shows its own lock and dam
entries.body: Pick a pool on the Arkansas River page and the Tailwaters tab shows that lock and dam alone, laid out like the Bull Shoals dam card: the pool against normal, the release, what it means below the dam, and Upstream and Downstream to step along the river.

entries.title: Signing out clears your saved waters and plans from the phone
entries.body: When you sign out, your saved waters, plans and kept trips leave that phone and come back when you sign in, so a buddy who borrows it sees none of them. Settings also has Sign out everywhere, which ends your sign-in on every phone and computer.

entries.title: Arkansas River pools, tailwaters and locks on the map
entries.body: The Arkansas River page now lists its twelve pools, each with its level and its dam's release. Pick one to see its lock and dam, or open the Tailwaters tab. Each lock and dam has its own pin on the map, and a pool's Map button goes to its dam, not the middle of the river.

entries.title: Arkansas River pools in the menu and on Generation & Levels
entries.body: Under Generation & Levels in the menu, Arkansas River · All pools opens every lock and dam on the river, with each pool's level and release. Search by pool, dam or town to find one.

entries.title: Save an Arkansas River pool and see its latest read
entries.body: Save a pool from its card to see its latest Corps read on Saved, and open it on the Arkansas River page from there.

entries.title: What's new says where a change lives, and takes your word on it
entries.body: Every note here now names the part of the app it changed, with a filter at the top and a link into that part. A picture rides along where one helps. Something off since an update? Tell us under the note: the feedback carries the change and the build you are on, so we can tie the two together.

image.alt: What's new on a phone: chips for the parts of the app along the top, then the newest note with its part, its Open link and Something off? Tell us

entries.title: Arkansas River pool levels now update every hour
entries.body: The Arkansas River pool cards on Waters now read the Corps every hour: each lock and dam's pool level, which way it moved over the day and the dam's release, with the time of its own reading. A pool that misses an hour says how old its reading is.

image.alt: One Arkansas River pool card on Waters on a phone: Trimble Pool rising, its level against normal pool and the dam's 24-hour release

entries.title: Dam generation on the map
entries.body: On the Live Waters Map, Beaver, Bull Shoals, Norfork and Greers Ferry now show how many units are running and whether the water is off, partial or full, with the reading's age. Tap a dam for the tailwater read without leaving the map.

entries.title: Arkansas River pool cards turn over for a tip
entries.body: Each Arkansas River pool card on Waters now turns over for what today's level means on the water, a tip for below the dam and a fact with its source. Share sends the pool's level and release with the time the Corps read it.

entries.title: Quick links on your profile, and plans you tap anywhere
entries.body: Your profile has a row of quick links that stays in reach as you scroll: Fishing plans with what waits on you, Buddies, My days, Tanks and Saved. A fishing plan now shows its day as a calendar tile with the time beside it, and tapping anywhere on it opens the conversation.

entries.title: Fishing plans: answer an ask in one tap
entries.body: The badge on your picture now opens Fishing plans when a buddy asks or answers. Each plan shows the day and time with I'm in, Can't make it or Suggest another time, plus your messages. Once you're both in, Add to calendar saves it.

entries.title: Every Arkansas River lock and dam, from Trimble to Norrell
entries.body: The Arkansas River pools on Waters now cover all twelve locks and dams in Arkansas. Each read pool shows its level and its dam's release over the last day, and the Ormond pool opens Arkansas River at Morrilton. Two dams with no Corps reading show their facts only.

image.alt: The Arkansas River band on Waters on a phone: the pools listed upstream to downstream, each card with its pool level and the dam's release

entries.title: Arkansas River pools say when they were read
entries.body: The Arkansas River pool cards on Waters now show the day the Corps reading was taken once it is more than a few hours old, instead of Rising or Falling. Each card opens a page: Lake Dardanelle its own, the other pools the Arkansas River.

entries.title: Get your water's read every Friday, from the water's page
entries.body: Under a water's read, type your email and tap Go. The 6-digit code makes your free account and the Friday read box starts checked; you can clear it. A new box asks if you want to hear when a guide on your water has a day open. In the game, a signed-out read now offers to save your stamps to an account.

entries.title: Sign in brings you back to what you tapped
entries.body: Tap a box on a species page, the game's sign-up, Start your Tackle Box, or a buddy's link while signed out and, after the code, you land on that page, not the Tackle Box. A page that needs an account now opens sign-in and says why, instead of dropping you on the home page.

image.alt: The sign-in box on a phone after opening Profile while signed out: it says Sign in to open your profile above the email field

entries.title: Tap a day on a buddy's calendar to plan it
entries.body: On a buddy's card, tap any day from today on. The day opens with the read for your water, their hours beside yours and the bite window. Ask them sends a text to that buddy, and Plan this day saves the day and adds it to your calendar.

entries.title: Ask a buddy about a day, right in the app
entries.body: On a buddy's calendar, open a day and tap Ask. They see it under Asked you to fish on their Buddies card, with a count on their profile picture, and See the day opens your card on that day. Text still sends it from your phone. A buddy of under two weeks wears a New buddy tag.

entries.title: Setting up is three pictures and a name
entries.body: Pick where you fish from a picture, tap the fish you want most, say how you like to fish, then add a name. Each tap saves, so you can come back. Your fish is your picture now, and it hatches into your tank at the end.

entries.title: See the fishing on your calendar, and each day's forecast
entries.body: Conditions on your free-days calendar now marks each day with an icon: a fish for a hot bite, the forecast sky, wind or storm warnings, and full or new moons. A line counts the hot days ahead and how many fall on days you're free. Tap a day for its forecast and fishing window.

entries.title: Your calendar starts at this week
entries.body: The free-days calendar on your profile and on a buddy's card no longer fills the screen with weeks that are already over. This month now opens on the week you're in, so the days still ahead sit higher on the screen.

entries.title: Set up your business account from one email link
entries.body: We can now email your business a setup link. Sign in with the address it was sent to and tap Link my account, and that login runs your page: your days, trips, prices and requests. The link works once, for a week.

entries.title: The buddy badge waits until you see Buddies
entries.body: Opening your profile no longer clears the buddy count before you reach the Buddies card. It clears once the card has been on screen for a moment, and the people who were waiting say New for that visit.

entries.title: The home page's guide card opens the guide's page
entries.body: The Outfitters & Guides card on the home page now opens the business's page, where their days, trips and doors are, instead of calling or leaving the app. On a guide's page, Check availability opens the booking panel.

entries.title: Every guide on a listing posts their own open days
entries.body: Set up your listing now asks whose days you're marking, so each guide keeps their own. Saving another step no longer refreshes the posted date: tick These days still hold when they do, and step 4 tells you when anglers stop seeing old days.

entries.title: Reopen asks first, and the Guide desk waits for each save
entries.body: On the Guide desk, Reopen on a booked trip now asks before it frees the day. A form stays open until the save comes back, says what went wrong in plain words if it didn't, and past trips no longer offer buttons. Every button is large enough for a thumb.

entries.title: A water's Partner Spotlight is local
entries.body: On a water's Signals tab, the Partner Spotlight now shows only the businesses that work that water, nearest first, with where they are. It stays put until you swipe.

image.alt: The Partner Spotlight on a water page on a phone: an outfitter that works this water, how far down from the dam it is, and arrows to swipe to the next

entries.title: Page through a guide's calendar month by month
entries.body: A guide's booking panel now shows one month at a time with Previous and Next, out to the last day they posted, so a spring trip they opened in the autumn is there to pick. Each month says how many days are open.

entries.title: Pick the water and the day when you plan a trip
entries.body: The day sheet on your profile no longer assumes your home water. Change the water to any lake, river or tailwater (your saved ones first) and the read follows it, pick any day up to a year out, or tap Plan a day. Ask them now names the water.

entries.title: Search and filter Outfitters & Guides
entries.body: Outfitters & Guides now has the same search and filters as Waters and Species: pick a kind, search by name, town, water or guide, filter by water or what you need, and switch between cards and a compact list. The order stays by name.

image.alt: Outfitters & Guides on a phone: kind chips with icons, a search box, the Any water and What you need filters, and the Cards or List switch

entries.title: New buddies arrive with a name and can share their days
entries.body: Saying yes to a buddy link now asks for your name first, so your buddy never sees "An angler", and a ticked box shows your free days to your buddies. If your days are set to Only me, your Buddies card and theirs say so, with one tap to show them.

entries.title: Sponsors show at the top of the water they work
entries.body: A sponsored business now shows at the top of each water page it works, with its logo. The map is now an icon beside Share, so the top of the page has more room. Where several sponsor one water, the first changes each visit and the rest are a swipe away.

image.alt: The top of the White River below Bull Shoals Dam page on a phone, with a sponsor's logo and the word Sponsored under the pills

entries.title: Put your own photo and cover on your profile
entries.body: Tap the camera on your profile to add your photo, or Cover to set the picture behind your name and slide it up or down. Your photo shows in the top bar and on your buddies' view of you, and the location and camera details come off before it uploads.

entries.title: A guide's booking panel keeps your trip in view
entries.body: On a guide's page the doors now take one row at the foot of the panel, so the trip you picked stays in sight. A day opened from a card or the Friday email opens the panel on that day, and a day that was booked or has passed says so instead of vanishing.

entries.title: Pick how many anglers and see that trip's own price
entries.body: On a guide's page that prices by party size, choose 2 or 3 anglers once: every trip shows that party's price, the request and your message say how many of you are coming, and their rates show one row per trip instead of one per party.

entries.title: A buddy invite now explains itself
entries.body: Someone you invite now reads what Pocket Fishing Guide is and the three steps from their side, then sets up a profile right after saying yes, so you see their name and the days they can fish. Opening your own link shows what your buddy will see.

entries.title: A guide's page now says when your trip request was sent
entries.body: After you text, call or email a guide from their page, the panel says what you asked for and where it lives next: Your trips, or sign in to keep it there. Tapping twice never sends the same ask twice, and signed in, you choose whether the guide sees your angler profile.

entries.title: Tap a lure on a species or water page to open it
entries.body: The lures and baits on a species page, in the tackle box and on a water's Techniques tab now open when you tap them: a big picture of the lure on the fish's water, why it works, the water it does best in, and How-To and Shop.

entries.title: Tap a day on your free-days calendar to open it
entries.body: Your free-days calendar now opens a day when you tap it: who's free, the read and Ask them, with a row to mark that one day. To mark many days at once, switch to Edit my days, then Save.

entries.title: Buddy invites arrive as one message with a new card
entries.body: A buddy invite sent by text now shows up once: your note and one preview card, not the card twice. The card shows a river, your name and a small day chart of when the bite lands while you're both free.

entries.title: Angler reports say whether they were verified at the water
entries.body: Each angler report on a water's Reports tab and the weekly board now carries the label the submit sheet promised: Verified at the water when the report came with a fresh location fix there, otherwise Unverified. Your tank also stops counting reports that were turned down.

entries.title: Sponsors on species pages and the weekly report
entries.body: A sponsored guide now shows on the page for a fish found where they guide, with the water named. On the weekly report, a sponsored business on a water in that week's edition shows with its own river note, posted from its profile and dated.

entries.title: See a buddy's free days on a calendar
entries.body: A buddy's card now shows when they can fish as a month calendar instead of a long list: their free days filled in, yours marked underneath, the days you're both free ringed in green and the best one starred.

entries.title: A hello from the founder when you join
entries.body: When you finish setting up, Corey, who built Pocket Fishing Guide, asks to be your fishing buddy. Say yes and you see each other's free days; Not now is fine, nobody is told, and the ask never comes back.

entries.title: Buddy's tips on the Go-Fishing cards
entries.body: After you pick a fish in Go-Fishing, the best read gets Buddy's take beside it: a few tips for that fish and what it does this season, swipe for the next. Pick the wrong fish and Buddy still leaves you a tip on the one you chose.

entries.title: Keep a guided trip for later, or share it
entries.body: On a guide's page, pick a trip and its day shows as one card with what the morning or afternoon is like and the trout you may meet. Tap Keep to hold it on your Saved page, or Share to send it to a fishing buddy.

entries.title: Name who a buddy link is for
entries.body: Invite a buddy now asks who it's for, so Links you sent shows Rick waiting and Erin said yes instead of five identical rows. Only you see the name. Send again makes a fresh link for the same person; links without a name fold into one row you can take back at once.

entries.title: Open a buddy's profile to see their fish tanks and catches
entries.body: Tap a buddy's name on your Buddies card to see their fish tanks, home water, when they're free and, if they share them, their catches with photos. You choose what your buddies see in Settings, under What your buddies see.

entries.title: Guide pages show what a half day looks like
entries.body: A guide's page now lays out the morning half, the evening half and the full day on the day's real sunrise and sunset, with their prices and the next open day for each. On the White, the trout year shows what each season brings, with a source for every fact.

entries.title: See the buddy links you sent, and take one back
entries.body: Your Buddies card now lists the links you sent: still open, used and by whom, taken back or expired. Sent one to the wrong person? Tap Take back and it stops working. A buddy request that waits 30 days now drops off on its own.

entries.title: Your week on Pocket Fishing Guide, first on your profile
entries.body: Businesses now see their week at the top of the Guide view: how often anglers saw them, opened their card, tapped a door and asked for a day, each with last week beside it, a bar for every day, where anglers found them, and one next thing to do.

entries.title: Remove a buddy, and say yes to an invite with a tap
entries.body: You can now remove a buddy from the menu on their row without blocking them; you stop seeing each other's free days and they are not told. An invite link now waits for you to tap Say yes, so a link passed along in a group text cannot add the wrong person.

entries.title: Signing in is sturdier: a button and a 6-digit code
entries.body: The sign-in email now opens a page with one Sign in button, so an email app that checks links can no longer use yours up first. The same email has a 6-digit code you can type in the sign-in box, handy when the email is on your phone and you are on a computer.

entries.title: Mark free days up to a year ahead
entries.body: Your open-days calendar now shows one month at a time with big Previous and Next buttons and a Go to month list, so you can mark days as far as a year out. Every weekend fills the month you are looking at. Guides can post a year of open days too.

entries.title: Tap a day to see if the bite lines up with your crew
entries.body: A day on the 14-day calendar or your open days now opens one sheet: the day as a timeline with the bite window, your time and each buddy's, one line saying who it suits, and Ask them. Your open days get a Buddies or Conditions view and the best days together up top.

entries.title: See your business in the app before you sign up
entries.body: The partner page now lets a guide, lodge, marina, boat rental or tackle shop pick what they are, type their name and see their listing card, the lead they would get and what each plan includes.

entries.title: One calendar for you and your buddies
entries.body: Your buddies' free days now sit on your own calendar as dots in their colors. Tick who to count, or ask for only the days you're all free; the best shared day is named. Weekends and holidays are marked, a pip says how your home water reads for two weeks, and tapping a day shows who's free.

entries.title: Your listing and the console, one tap under your name
entries.body: A guide business or an admin now finds their page, Set up your listing and the console right under their name on the profile, not at the bottom of the page. Saved & planned shows your first three and a See all link to the full list.

entries.title: Your buddies show when they're free
entries.body: Each buddy on your profile now shows the days they've marked free and the days you're both free, with the best one named. A buddy who runs a guide service carries a Guide tag that opens their page. Block and Report sit behind the three dots.

entries.title: A simpler open-days card
entries.body: Who sees your days sits at the top, the picked days read as one line that opens to the list, and setting up a profile asks for one name.

entries.title: Fish with a buddy
entries.body: Invite someone you fish with by link. When they tap it and sign in, you're buddies: each of you can see the days the other marks free, never where you are. The Buddies card is on your profile; a number on your avatar says who is waiting on you.

entries.title: Mark the days you could fish
entries.body: Your profile has a six-week calendar: all day, a morning or an afternoon. They stay yours unless you switch them to My buddies.

entries.title: Nudges are off until you say so
entries.body: Nothing is sent unless you pick a cadence and a channel. Settings keeps the same switch.

entries.title: Guides: your open days from the calendar you already keep
entries.body: Make a calendar named PFG Open days, add an all-day Open (or Open AM, Open PM) on each day you can guide, and paste its iCal address on the Open days step of Set up your listing. It is read every hour.

entries.title: Guides: your week in one line
entries.body: The Guide view on your profile says how often your listing was seen, opened and had a door tapped, and which surface sent anglers to you. Counts only; no visitor is kept.

entries.title: Guides: evaluate a request before you answer, and record the deposit
entries.body: Each request on your desk opens to what the angler saw and asked for, the day's season bands and your deposit policy; Confirm prefills the posted price, and a deposit you received is recorded with its date.

entries.title: A guide's page shows the water they work, now
entries.body: Under the business's name, one card per dam that sets their water, with the same status the dam cards print.
